core: Both communities run a check that compares a model's text output against another reference text — either a repeated run of the same prompt or a set of worked few-shot examples — looking for verbatim, word-for-word overlap that shouldn't be there. Rather than a simple pass/fail, they quantify it: the share of sampled items showing matching or copied phrasing is reported as a percentage, and that rate is used to judge how much of the observed behavior reflects real content generation versus artifacts of repeated or copied text.
quote_1: same exact prompt, same session, submitted twice. Temperature's pinned to zero on paper, but outputs diverged by about 6% token-for-token, and once by a full different citation.
quote_2: The ⟦T2⟧ identified inappropriate verbatim carryover in 9.6% of free-form explanations, despite correct final tool outputs.
